headline: Operation Five Phases — Complete
message:
You now understand what actually happens in a professional penetration test — from the first signed document to the final report delivery.

Ravi's shock at spending an entire first day on paperwork makes sense now. The scope document, the Rules of Engagement, the authorization letter — these are not bureaucratic overhead. They are the legal and professional foundation that makes everything else possible. Without them, every action in Phases 2 through 4 is potentially criminal. With them, every action is authorised, traceable, and professionally defensible.

Yahoo's 3 billion compromised accounts show what happens when security reviews are treated as compliance checkboxes rather than genuine investigations. A real VAPT engagement — one that examined authentication systems, data-at-rest protections, and anomaly detection capabilities — would have surfaced the same weaknesses that attackers exploited for two years undetected.

The five phases now have meaning beyond labels: Scoping is the contract. Reconnaissance is the research. Scanning is the catalogue. Exploitation is the proof. Reporting is the product. Together, they constitute a professional engagement — one that produces findings organisations can act on, and one you can conduct with legal protection and professional confidence.

Review Flashcards — PTES phases, passive vs active recon, and CVSS score contextualisation appear in CEH and Security+ certification questions
